headline: Banks post real earnings beats (AKBL +25%, BAFL +27%) while oil and a fresh current-account deficit keep the macro backdrop tense.
summary: PSX closed slightly green Friday (176,094, +0.31%) as H1 earnings season delivered real bank wins: Askari Bank's profit jumped 25% YoY with a fresh Rs2 dividend, and Bank Alfalah confirmed a 27% YoY profit rise. That's against a genuinely tense backdrop though — Brent is still ~24% above its one-month base on Strait of Hormuz tensions, Pakistan's FY26 current account has flipped to a deficit, and FX reserves have fallen three straight weeks. The desk's geo-risk gauge reads 65/100, 'elevated.' Net read: banks are earning their spot on real numbers, but it's not a green light to chase broadly — smaller size, patience, and stick to names with confirmed catalysts behind them.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: H1 results season is delivering real beats — AKBL profit +25% YoY with a Rs2 dividend, BAFL +27% YoY — and the SBP's held 11.5% rate removes near-term policy uncertainty.

sectors.name: E&P (OGDC/PPL/MARI)
sectors.why: Brent is still ~24% above its one-month base even after this week's partial Hormuz de-escalation — a direct revenue tailwind that macro.json and the geo-risk radar both flag as the one sector benefiting from the oil spike.

sectors.name: OMCs
sectors.why: Daily ex-depot fuel-price revisions plus a newly confirmed FY26 current-account deficit squeeze margin timing and keep circular-debt risk alive.

sectors.name: Refineries
sectors.why: Exposed to oil-price whipsaw as Hormuz shipping flows recover only partially — market estimates put traffic back to just ~30-35% of pre-crisis levels.

sectors.name: Cement
sectors.why: Energy-cost sensitivity stays high; Maple Leaf's FY26 profit rose a modest 9% YoY on 24% higher revenue, showing the sector is squeezed, not broken.

sectors.name: Textiles / exporters
sectors.why: A confirmed FY26 current-account deficit and still-elevated Hormuz-related freight and insurance costs weigh on exporter margins.

watchlist.angle: H1 2026 profit jumped 25% YoY to Rs13.35bn with a fresh Rs2/share dividend declared today — a confirmed impact-4 catalyst that triggered this cycle's full-pipeline run. Fundamentals read 'attractive': P/E 6.7 (cheapest third of PSX), forward P/E 5.83 below trailing, 4.85% dividend yield on a covered 46% payout. The desk's backtested 'Reclaim 200-day' strategy on AKBL has a supportive record (56% hit rate over 25 trades, 80% out-of-sample) though it hasn't fired yet — AKBL's last close (Jul 30, pre-announcement) sat right on its 50-day average.
watchlist.risk: AKBL's own DPS filing shows a conflicting Q2-only PAT of Rs6.57bn/EPS 4.53 that doesn't cleanly reconcile with the Rs13.35bn H1 headline, and today's price reaction to the news isn't in the technical data yet (last close predates the announcement).

watchlist.angle: The desk's live signal stack has BML's 'Volume leads price' (OBV divergence) triggering now — high confidence, backtest-proven: 97% hit rate over 89 trades, +5.1% net expectancy, still 83% out-of-sample. Fundamentals back it up — 'attractive' rating, P/E 6.44 (cheap third of PSX), 32% net margin. Results are on the earnings calendar for today (2026-07-31).
watchlist.risk: No dividend — this is a pure price-return thesis, and it's firing the same day results are due, so a miss could break the pattern fast.

watchlist.angle: Q2 2026 profit confirmed up 27% YoY / 7.6% QoQ (Rs10bn PAT, EPS 3.22), resolving an earlier DPS-filing mismatch after two sources corroborated the figure. Fundamentals read 'attractive': P/E 5.72 (cheapest third), 10.4% dividend yield on a sustainable 57% payout, 17% net margin.
watchlist.risk: No live technical trigger backing this one yet — the case rests on the earnings beat and cheap valuation alone, and no dividend was confirmed alongside these results.

UBL book closure begins; Rs16/share dividend (3.38% yield)
SBP weekly FX reserves print — watched for whether the third straight weekly decline (to $17.03bn) extends
SBP MPC — second FY27 monetary policy decision

risks: Geo-risk gauge is pinned at 65/100 'elevated' with conflict/escalation and energy-shock stress both maxed out — any Hormuz re-escalation hits PSX fast via oil and the rupee.

Pakistan's FY26 current account has confirmed a swing to deficit ($139mn) and FX reserves have fallen three straight weeks to $17.03bn — a live external-account vulnerability, not resolved by today's tactical oil pullback.
This week's earnings data is unusually noisy — AKBL's H1 headline and EFERT's Q2 headline both conflict with their own DPS filings — so some of today's 'good news' isn't fully reconciled yet.
